sources.title: Live birth outcomes after first donor oocyte embryo transfer: a comparison by treatment pathways in poor prognosis patients
sources.journal: Journal of Assisted Reproduction and Genetics
sources.claim: 157 donor-first and 196 IVF-first patients; live birth after first donor transfer 59.2% vs 53.1% (similar); across all donor transfers 50.4% vs 49.2%; donor-first reached live birth faster, 13.2 vs 21.0 months.
sources.quote: The live birth rate after the first donor oocyte embryo transfer was similar between groups (DONOR-1st 59.2% vs IVF-1st 53.1%, p = 0.24) ... 13.2 ± 9.9 months versus 21.0 ± 13.7 months (p < 0.01)

sources.title: Cumulative live birth rates and number of oocytes retrieved in women of advanced age. A single centre analysis including 4500 women >=38 years old
sources.claim: Cumulative live birth rate per retrieval with own eggs: 25.9% at 38-39, 16.4% at 40-41, 7% at 42-43, 1.2% from 44; more eggs = higher CLBR, clearest up to 41.
sources.quote: CLBRs significantly decrease with increasing age among women >=38 years of age (25.9% at 38-39 years, 16.4% at 40-41 years, 7% at 42-43 years and 1.2% from 44 years onwards)

sources.title: Which assisted reproductive technology (ART) treatment strategy is the most clinically and cost-effective for women of advanced maternal age: a Markov model
sources.claim: Model: standard autologous ART cumulative live birth 45% at 35 falling to 1.6% at 45; donor ART had the highest cumulative live birth rate; PGT-A and donor ART had higher treatment costs.
sources.quote: standard autologous ART has the lowest cumulative live birth rate of 45% at age 35 ... decreasing to 1.6% by age 45 years ... PGT-A and donor ART were associated with higher treatment costs

sources.title: New national outcome data on fresh versus cryopreserved donor oocytes
sources.claim: 30,160 US donor egg IVF cycles: live birth per recipient cycle start 51.1% fresh vs 39.7% frozen donor eggs.
sources.quote: Fresh donor oocytes produced significantly higher live birth rates per recipient cycle start than cryopreserved donor oocytes (51.1% vs 39.7%)

sources.title: Evidence-based outcomes after oocyte cryopreservation for donor oocyte IVF and planned oocyte cryopreservation: a guideline
sources.claim: No significant difference in per-transfer pregnancy rates with frozen vs fresh donor eggs; frozen donor eggs are a reasonable option; more live-birth data needed.
sources.quote: There are no significant differences in per transfer pregnancy rates with cryopreserved vs. fresh donor oocytes ... previously cryopreserved donor oocytes are a reasonable option

sources.title: Is the risk of preeclampsia higher in donor oocyte pregnancies? A systematic review and meta-analysis
sources.claim: Egg donation associated with higher preeclampsia risk than IVF with own eggs in singleton pregnancies (OR 4.50).
sources.quote: statistically significant association between egg donation and onset of preeclampsia (OR 4.50; 95% CI: 3.28-6.19; p<0.0001)

sources.title: Pregnancy outcomes decline in recipients over age 44: an analysis of 27,959 fresh donor oocyte IVF cycles from SART
sources.claim: 27,959 fresh donor egg cycles: recipient outcomes stable before 45; lower rates at 45-49 and 50+.
sources.quote: donor oocyte recipients have stable rates of pregnancy outcomes before age 45

sources.title: First live births after adipose-derived stem cells and platelet-rich plasma intraovarian administration
sources.claim: A 46-year-old with DOR conceived naturally six months after adipose-PRP and delivered at 47; a 45-year-old with multiple failed IVF had a birth from her only euploid embryo made three months after treatment.
sources.quote: Case 1, a 46-year-old with diminished ovarian reserve and prior miscarriage ... delivered a healthy infant at age 47

sources.title: Egg donation (fact sheet)
sources.claim: Donors usually 21-34; recipient takes estrogen then progesterone; transfer 3-5 days after fertilization; success not considered related to recipient age; 53.5% average birth rate per transfer with fresh donor eggs (2020 SART/CDC).
sources.quote: an average birth rate per embryo transfer of 53.5% for all egg donor programs using fresh eggs
